responses.m1_analysis: Yes, the revised request improved the response because the robot was able to identify the specific blue cup. One important difference is that the original example did not provide an alternative in case the robot could not move the cup or did not have the capability to pick it up. My revised request specifically instructed the robot to report what it observes and explain its limitations if it cannot pick up the cup.
responses.m2_analysis: I chose the Identify task and my revised request produced a better answer for that goal than the original request. One specific difference is that the revised answer not only identified the tool in the foreground as a measuring tape but also explained the visible features that helped identify it. These features included the length of the tape, the markings on it, and the presence of a hole in the tape.
responses.m3_analysis: My prompt did not perform well compared to the expected route. The robot made only 12 successful moves out of 50 actions and did not reach the goal. It also had 21 blocked moves and 17 STOP actions and after reaching position (1,1) it kept trying to move UP instead of following the next instruction to move RIGHT. This shows that even though I provided specific directions the model still struggled to follow the route and avoid repeating blocked moves. Its main limitation is that it does not consistently follow the planned directions when making decisions at each step.
responses.final_synthesis: Working through all three missions, I learned that giving instructions to a robot needs to be precise and descriptive. In mission 1 adding instructions for the robot to explain its limitations helped make the response more useful when it could not pick up the blue cup. In mission 2 asking it to identify the measuring tape and describe its visible features made the answer more specific. In mission 3 even though I gave the robot step by step directions it only made 12 successful moves out of 50 and never reached the goal. This showed me that clear prompts and visible evidence can improve responses, but they do not guarantee that the robot will follow instructions correctly. One limitation is that the model can still make incorrect decisions when choosing actions.
responses.final.course_reflection: This activity gave me a better understanding of how foundation models can be used to give instructions to robots and guide their actions. I learned that prompts need to be clear and specific because the model does not always understand what we want it to do. What stood out to me was how changing the wording of a request affected the model's responses. For example, in mission 1 adding instructions to explain its limitations made the response more useful when it could not pick up the blue cup. In mission 2 asking the model to identify the measuring tape and describe its visible features helped it give a more specific answer. However, in mission 3 even with detailed step by step directions the robot struggled to follow the route and was unable to reach the goal. This showed me that a detailed prompt does not always guarantee the robot will follow the instructions correctly. The activity made me more interested in learning how to improve the way robots understand instructions and interact with their surroundings. I also think it is important to make sure robots act safely and explain their limitations instead of making incorrect decisions. Overall, this activity helped me understand that getting useful robot behavior involves more than just giving instructions. We also need to check the model's responses and make sure its actions match what we asked it to do.

controls.control_live_language_custom_prompt: Inspect the blue cup on the shelf and move it to the desk if you have the capability to pick it up. If you can’t pick it up or don’t see the blue cup then report what you observe and explain the limitation.
controls.control_live_vision_custom_prompt: Identify the tool in the foreground of the workbench and describe the visible features that helped you identify it. If you are unsure about the tool's identity explain what makes it unclear instead of guessing.
controls.control_robot_custom_prompt: Move the robot to the blue target at (11,1). Follow the route step by step and don't skip any part. Start at (1,7) and move UP one space at a time until you reach (1,1). Then move RIGHT one space at a time until you reach (7,1). Next, move DOWN until you reach (7,7). After that, move RIGHT until you reach (11,7). Finally, move UP until you reach (11,1). Keep checking your current coordinates after each move. If you hit a wall, don't keep repeating the same move or choose STOP. Try another direction that is open. Only stop once you reach the blue target.
